Link budget¶

Summary¶

functions.link_budget is the integrating module of the GNSS-R signal chain: it turns a set of transmitter / receiver / reflection-point states into a received power, a thermal-noise floor, and the derived figures of merit (\(C/N_0\), SNR). It owns three responsibilities:

  1. Geometry – build_bistatic_geometry() reduces the raw Tx, Rx and surface states to the per-sample directions, ranges and angles that every downstream physics model needs (BistaticGeometry).

  2. Scattering hand-off – compute_reflection_link_budget() asks a Target (by default OceanTarget) for the radar cross section at that geometry, sizing the illuminated area for distributed (area-extensive) returns.

  3. The link equation – compute_bistatic_link_budget() evaluates the bistatic radar equation and the receiver noise model, returning a fully populated link-budget dictionary.

The module carries receiver-side losses only. The GNSS transmit EIRP is a property of the transmitting signal and lives in Constants.GNSS_EIRP_DBW per (constellation, band); it is passed in as tx_eirp_dbw and is never a link-budget configuration knob. Both analysis modes consume this module: Reflection and BRP call it per reflection, and MovingTargetDetection calls it per band.

Interface¶

The public surface is two data classes plus three functions. Vectors follow the simulator convention: satellite state vectors are (3, n) and reflection points are (n, 3).

Note

The illuminated-area model has three modes, selected by the settings: the steered-beam footprint (default), one delay-Doppler resolution cell (delay_doppler_cell_enabled; see functions.delay_doppler), or a patch-integrated footprint (ocean_patch_integration_enabled). The first two are mutually exclusive.

Detailed Module Description¶

Bistatic geometry¶

For each sample, build_bistatic_geometry() forms the incoming and outgoing propagation unit vectors and the outward surface normal:

(17)¶\[\hat{n}_{tx2s} = \frac{S - T}{\lVert S - T \rVert}, \qquad \hat{n}_{s2rx} = \frac{R - S}{\lVert R - S \rVert}, \qquad \hat{n}_{surf} = \frac{N}{\lVert N \rVert}\]

with Tx, Rx and surface positions \(T, R, S\) and the (unnormalised) surface normal \(N\). The slant ranges are \(R_t = \lVert S - T \rVert\) and \(R_r = \lVert R - S \rVert\), and the three angles follow from dot products:

(18)¶\[\cos\left(\theta_i\right) = -\,\hat{n}_{tx2s}\cdot\hat{n}_{surf}, \qquad \cos\left(\theta_s\right) = \hat{n}_{s2rx}\cdot\hat{n}_{surf}, \qquad \cos\left(\beta\right) = -\,\hat{n}_{tx2s}\cdot\hat{n}_{s2rx}\]

The bistatic angle \(\beta\) is 0 deg for backscatter, \(2\theta_i\) for the specular geometry, and 180 deg for pure forward scatter. Any invalid sample (NaN input, zero range, zero-length normal) propagates as NaN rather than raising, so a single bad reflection never poisons a batch.

The link equation¶

compute_bistatic_link_budget() evaluates the simplified bistatic radar equation,

(19)¶\[P_r = \frac{\mathrm{EIRP}\;G_r\,\lambda^2\,\sigma}{(4\pi)^3\,R_t^2\,R_r^2\,L}\]

where \(\mathrm{EIRP} = P_t G_t\) is the transmit EIRP [W], \(G_r\) the receiver gain along the look direction, \(\lambda = c/f\) the carrier wavelength, \(\sigma\) the target RCS [m^2] supplied by the Target, and \(L\) the lumped receiver-side loss (system_losses_db + polarization_losses_db). The two one-way free-space path losses are reported separately,

(20)¶\[\mathrm{FSPL}_{1\text{-way}} = 20\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{4\pi R}{\lambda}\right),\]

for the Tx->surface and surface->Rx legs.

Illuminated area and the distributed target¶

For a distributed (area-extensive) return such as the ocean, the RCS scales with an illuminated area. With an antenna present, the receiver auto-steers to the reflection, so rx_gain_dbi is the steered-beam peak directivity and the beam solid angle \(4\pi/G_r\) projects to a ground footprint:

(21)¶\[A_\mathrm{fp} = \frac{4\pi}{G_r}\,\frac{R_r^2}{\cos\left(\theta_s\right)}.\]

The projection angle is the receiver scattering angle \(\theta_s\), not the transmitter incidence angle \(\theta_i\). The cosine is clipped to [0.05, 1.0] to bound the grazing-angle blow-up. This area is then passed to Target.compute_rcs so the target owns how it is used. When delay_doppler_cell_enabled, the area is replaced by a single delay-Doppler resolution cell (capped at \(A_\mathrm{fp}\)); when ocean_patch_integration_enabled, the ocean clutter is integrated patch-by-patch over the footprint and converted to an equivalent centre RCS. With antenna=None no area is imposed here and the target falls back to its own geometric area.

Thermal noise and C/N0¶

When noise settings are supplied (moving-target mode), the module forms the ideal thermal floor

(22)¶\[N_0 = k\,T_\mathrm{sys}, \qquad N = k\,T_\mathrm{sys}\,B, \qquad C/N_0 = \frac{P_r}{N_0}, \qquad \mathrm{SNR} = \frac{P_r}{N}\]

with Boltzmann constant \(k\), system noise temperature \(T_\mathrm{sys}\) and noise bandwidth \(B\). \(C/N_0\) is the bandwidth-independent figure; snr_rf_db is the pre-correlation SNR in \(B\) and deliberately excludes the code-despreading / coherent-integration processing gain. The detector adds that gain when it forms the SINR (next subsection). Area coverage supplies no noise settings, so the noise block is emitted as NaN and the geometric path never depends on a floor it does not model.

Coherent processing gain¶

The figures above are pre-correlation: they weigh the received power against the full-bandwidth thermal floor \(N = k\,T_\mathrm{sys}\,B\). A GNSS receiver instead correlates the incoming signal against a local replica of the transmitted spread-spectrum (PRN) code and integrates. This despreading lifts a code-carrying signal out of the white thermal noise. coherent_processing_gain_linear() returns the linear gain

(23)¶\[G_p = \underbrace{B\,T_\mathrm{coh}}_{\text{coherent}}\;\underbrace{\sqrt{M}}_{\text{incoherent}}\]

with coherent integration time \(T_\mathrm{coh}\) (coherent_integration_time_s) and number of incoherent looks \(M\) (num_incoherent_looks). Coherent integration over \(T_\mathrm{coh}\) narrows the equivalent noise bandwidth to order \(1/T_\mathrm{coh}\), giving \(B\,T_\mathrm{coh}\). The additional \(\sqrt{M}\) represents the reduction in estimator standard deviation from averaging independent power looks. The detector expresses both effects as a single detection-equivalent noise scale

(24)¶\[N_\mathrm{eff} = \frac{N}{G_p} = \frac{k\,T_\mathrm{sys}}{T_\mathrm{coh}\,\sqrt{M}}\]

The bandwidth cancels algebraically. However, incoherent averaging does not reduce the mean thermal noise power by \(\sqrt{M}\); it reduces the fluctuation of an estimator. Consequently noise_power_effective_w and the resulting threshold comparison are a sensitivity approximation, not a literal post-detection mean-noise power or a probability-of-detection calculation. A rigorous detector would specify the statistic, false-alarm probability and signal/noise distributions.

The gain acts on the noise term only. The ocean clutter carries the same PRN code as the target, so it despreads with the same \(G_p\); the gain cancels in the signal-to-clutter ratio \(P_\mathrm{ship}/P_\mathrm{ocean}\) and merely lifts both returns above the thermal floor. The SINR formed in MovingTargetDetection is therefore the implemented detection metric

(25)¶\[\mathrm{SINR} = \frac{P_\mathrm{ship}}{P_\mathrm{ocean} + N_\mathrm{eff}}\]

so a long enough \(T_\mathrm{coh}\) moves the system from noise-limited (\(N_\mathrm{eff} > P_\mathrm{ocean}\)) to clutter-limited (\(N_\mathrm{eff} < P_\mathrm{ocean}\)): noise- vs clutter-limited is a receiver-setting choice, not a fixed property.

\(T_\mathrm{coh}\) is physically bounded by the navigation-data bit period and, over the sea, by the surface decorrelation time (a few ms for the diffuse return). The model applies \(G_p\) to the thermal noise and leaves the clutter at full strength – it assumes the clutter stays coherent over \(T_\mathrm{coh}\) (the conservative choice). A clutter return that decorrelates faster than \(T_\mathrm{coh}\) would gain less than a steady target, so a finer model would apply separate, coherence-time-limited gains to the ship and the ocean; that differential-coherence discriminator is not yet modelled.

API reference¶

class functions.link_budget.BistaticLinkBudgetSettings(system_losses_db, polarization_losses_db, ocean_wave_height_m, ocean_wind_speed_m_s, ocean_wind_direction_deg, ocean_sea_temperature_c, ocean_salinity_psu, ocean_inverse_wave_age, noise_bandwidth_hz=None, system_noise_temperature_k=None, detection_sinr_threshold_db=None, ocean_patch_integration_enabled=False, ocean_patch_grid_size=9, delay_doppler_cell_enabled=False, coherent_integration_time_s=None, num_incoherent_looks=1)[source]¶

Configuration values for the bistatic GNSS-R link budget.

Field-by-field source of truth for the [LINK BUDGET] + [OCEAN] INI sections; field names and units defined here mirror the INI keys. The physical ocean/loss fields are mandatory so a missing value raises instead of silently falling back. The INI loader is strict (missing keys raise); the thermal-noise + detection-threshold fields are consumed only by the moving-target detector and default to None (they are omitted from the area-coverage config, which is geometric). Patch-integration controls have conservative defaults and can be overridden from [LINK BUDGET]. Direct construction with settings=None is not accepted.

ATTRIBUTES:

system_losses_db: [float] Lumped implementation losses [dB] polarization_losses_db: [float] Receiver-side polarization mismatch losses [dB] ocean_wave_height_m: [float] Significant wave height H_s [m] (Rayleigh model uses sigma_h ~= H_s/4) ocean_wind_speed_m_s: [float] Wind speed at 10 m [m/s] (drives Cox-Munk slope variances) ocean_wind_direction_deg: [float] Wind direction (meteorological FROM bearing) [deg] ocean_sea_temperature_c: [float] Sea surface temperature [degC] ocean_salinity_psu: [float] Salinity (practical salinity units) [psu] ocean_inverse_wave_age: [float] Inverse wave age Omega_c [-] (0.84 fully developed; drives the Elfouhaily Bragg spectrum) noise_bandwidth_hz: [float | None] Thermal-noise bandwidth for SNR [Hz] (moving-target only; None for area coverage) system_noise_temperature_k:[float | None] Equivalent input/system noise temperature [K] (moving-target only) detection_sinr_threshold_db:[float | None] Ship detectability threshold for P_ship / (P_ocean + P_noise) [dB] (moving-target only) ocean_patch_integration_enabled:[bool] Enable footprint patch integration for antenna-limited ocean clutter. ocean_patch_grid_size: [int] Number of cells per tangent-plane footprint axis for patch integration. delay_doppler_cell_enabled:[bool] Use the delay-Doppler resolution cell (not the full footprint) as the distributed-clutter area. coherent_integration_time_s:[float | None] Coherent integration time T_coh [s]; sets the Doppler bin (1 / T_coh) of the cell. Required when the cell is enabled. num_incoherent_looks: [int] Independent incoherent looks M (>= 1); sqrt(M) is a detection-sensitivity approximation.

NOTE: GNSS transmitter EIRP is per-(constellation, band) and lives in Constants.GNSS_EIRP_DBW — it is not a link-budget config knob.

functions.link_budget.compute_bistatic_link_budget(range_tx_m, range_rx_m, rx_gain_dbi, rcs_m2, frequency_hz, tx_eirp_dbw, settings=None)[source]¶

Compute simplified bistatic GNSS-R received power from a precomputed RCS.

Pr = EIRP * G_rx * lambda^2 * sigma / ((4 pi)^3 * R_t^2 * R_r^2 * L).

fspl_sum_db is the sum of one-way FSPL terms (Tx->surface plus surface->Rx). bistatic_spreading_loss_db is the corresponding spreading term used in the simplified bistatic radar equation implementation.

  • range_rx_m (numpy.ndarray) – Distance reflection point to receiver [m].

  • rcs_m2 (numpy.ndarray) – Target RCS per sample [m^2]; supplied by a Target implementation.

  • frequency_hz (float) – Carrier frequency [Hz].

  • tx_eirp_dbw (float) – Transmitter EIRP for the specific (constellation, band) [dBW].

  • settings (dict or BistaticLinkBudgetSettings or None) – Rx-system link-budget settings.

Returns:

Link budget components and received power arrays.

Return type:

dict

functions.link_budget.coherent_processing_gain_linear(settings)[source]¶

Detection-equivalent gain used by the threshold metric: B * T_coh * sqrt(M).

Coherent integration over T_coh narrows the effective noise bandwidth from B to about 1 / T_coh (a gain of B * T_coh). M independent power looks reduce estimator standard deviation by approximately sqrt(M); they do not lower mean noise power. The combined value is therefore a sensitivity approximation rather than a full detector-statistics model. Returns 1.0 when no coherent integration time or noise bandwidth is set.

Parameters:

settings (dict | BistaticLinkBudgetSettings)

Return type:

float

Module Assumptions and Limitations¶

  • Receiver-side losses only. system_losses_db and polarization_losses_db lump into \(L\); the transmit EIRP is supplied per (constellation, band) from Constants.GNSS_EIRP_DBW.

  • Surface normals default to geocentric. Unless surface_normals_eci is supplied, the reflection position is used as the normal, which is exact only for a sphere. The elliptical-Earth path supplies WGS-84 ellipsoid normals (see ellipsoid_surface_normals_eci()).

  • Simplified point-target radar equation. Distributed-target physics enters only through \(\sigma\) and the illuminated area; multiple scattering and coherent speckle statistics are not modelled here.

  • Link-budget SNR is pre-correlation. snr_rf_db and cn0_db_hz report the raw RF link, before any despreading / integration gain. The moving-target detector applies the coherent and incoherent sensitivity factor \(B\,T_\mathrm{coh}\,\sqrt{M}\) in its threshold metric (see functions.link_budget.coherent_processing_gain_linear()). The \(\sqrt{M}\) part is an estimator-variance approximation, not a physical reduction of mean noise power.

  • Approximate footprint. \(4\pi/G_r\) treats peak directivity as an equivalent beam solid angle and projects it with \(\cos\theta_s\), clipped to [0.05, 1.0]. It is not an integration of the actual contour unless patch integration is enabled.

  • Incoherent-look metric. The \(\sqrt{M}\) term models sensitivity improvement through estimator variance. It must not be interpreted as a reduction in mean thermal noise power.

  • Isotropic fallback. antenna=None assumes a 0 dBi receiver and imposes no footprint area.

Validation and Tests¶

The module is regression-locked from pure geometry up to the end-to-end ocean physics:

Test module

What it pins

tests/test_bistatic_geometry.py

Zenith geometry gives all angles 0; the specular geometry gives \(\beta = 2\theta_i\); ranges; NaN propagation and shape validation.

tests/test_link_budget.py

compute_rx_look_direction_antenna_frame NaN guards and match to the manual rotation chain; the noise model is exactly \(kTB\); SNR and \(C/N_0\) derivations; doubling the bandwidth drops SNR by 3 dB but leaves \(C/N_0\) unchanged; non-positive noise settings raise; the area-coverage path yields NaN noise but finite power.

tests/test_link_budget_sanity.py

End-to-end through OceanTarget: finite Pr across incidence; the per-constellation EIRP plumbing produces the exact 5 dB Galileo-vs-GPS shift; forward specular exceeds oblique backscatter; received power and Bragg \(\sigma_0\) sit in deliberately broad plausibility envelopes. These are sanity bounds, not CYGNSS calibration.

tests/test_link_budget_golden.py

Golden-file regression against tests/golden/reference_link_budget.npz; any change in geometry, ocean physics or the link equation flips it red. Regenerate intentionally via tests/golden/regenerate_link_budget.py.

User Guide¶

The receiver-system parameters come from the [LINK BUDGET] INI section; the ocean sea-state fields come from [OCEAN]. Both feed BistaticLinkBudgetSettings. The loader is INI-strict (missing required keys raise).

Table 3: [LINK BUDGET] keys¶

Key

Meaning

system_losses_db

Lumped implementation loss (feedline, filter, ADC, correlator) [dB, >= 0].

polarization_losses_db

Receiver antenna polarization-mismatch loss (not the RHCP->LHCP reflection flip) [dB, >= 0].

noise_bandwidth_hz

Thermal-noise bandwidth \(B\) [Hz] (moving-target only).

system_noise_temperature_k

Equivalent system noise temperature \(T_\mathrm{sys}\) [K] (moving-target only).

detection_sinr_threshold_db

Ship detectability threshold for \(P_\mathrm{ship}/(P_\mathrm{ocean}+N)\) [dB].

ocean_patch_integration_enabled

Integrate ocean clutter patch-by-patch over the footprint instead of one scalar area.

ocean_patch_grid_size

Cells per footprint axis for that integration [3 .. 101].

delay_doppler_cell_enabled

Use one delay-Doppler resolution cell as the distributed-clutter area (mutually exclusive with patch integration).

coherent_integration_time_s

Coherent integration time \(T_\mathrm{coh}\) [s]; sets the cell Doppler bin \(1/T_\mathrm{coh}\) and the coherent processing gain \(B\,T_\mathrm{coh}\). Required when the cell is enabled.

num_incoherent_looks

Independent incoherent looks \(M\) (>= 1); applies a heuristic \(\sqrt{M}\) detection sensitivity improvement, not a reduction in mean noise power.

A minimal call (isotropic receiver, GPS L1, area-coverage-style settings):

import numpy as np
from functions.link_budget import BistaticLinkBudgetSettings, compute_reflection_link_budget

settings = BistaticLinkBudgetSettings(
    system_losses_db=2.0,
    polarization_losses_db=0.5,
    ocean_wave_height_m=1.5,
    ocean_wind_speed_m_s=7.0,
    ocean_wind_direction_deg=270.0,
    ocean_sea_temperature_c=10.0,
    ocean_salinity_psu=35.0,
    ocean_inverse_wave_age=0.84,
    noise_bandwidth_hz=2.0e6,
    system_noise_temperature_k=290.0,
)

lb = compute_reflection_link_budget(
    tx_positions_eci=tx,             # (3, n) GNSS Tx ECI positions [m]
    rx_positions_eci=rx,             # (3, n) LEO Rx ECI positions [m]
    rx_velocities_eci=rx_vel,        # (3, n) LEO Rx ECI velocities [m/s]
    reflection_positions_eci=surf,   # (n, 3) reflection points [m]
    incidence_deg=inc,               # (n,)  incidence angle [deg]
    antenna=None,                    # isotropic 0 dBi
    frequency_hz=1.57542e9,          # GPS L1
    tx_eirp_dbw=27.0,                # from Constants.GNSS_EIRP_DBW
    settings=settings,
)
print(lb["received_power_dbm"], lb["cn0_db_hz"])

References¶

  • Zavorotny, V. & Voronovich, A., “Scattering of GPS signals from the ocean with wind remote sensing application”, IEEE TGRS 38(2), 2000.

  • Ruf, C. et al., “A new paradigm in earth environmental monitoring with the CYGNSS small satellite constellation”, Scientific Reports 8, 2018.
